about: Free assessment tools shown at the top of the Assessment page. Every field is plain text. kind is a list drawn from Screening, Diagnostic, Progress monitoring and Questionnaire. Only list a tool when its free access has been checked on the publisher's own site, and say exactly what is free.

tools.name: DIBELS 8th Edition: Australasian version
tools.delivery: One-to-one. The Maze comprehension task can be given to a whole class.
tools.time: About one minute for each subtest, so a few minutes per student
tools.tells: Whether each student is on track in letter naming, phonemic segmentation, nonsense word reading, word reading, oral reading fluency and comprehension (Maze), and who is at risk of reading difficulty, including dyslexia.
tools.who: Whole year levels three times a year to find students who need more support, then more often for students in intervention to check that it is working.
tools.access: Free download
tools.note: This is the version adapted for Australia and New Zealand. Use it in place of the American materials.

tools.name: Year 1 Phonics Check
tools.by: Australian Government, on the Literacy Hub
tools.years: Year 1 (usually Term 3), Year 2 and older struggling readers
tools.tells: How well a student decodes real and made-up words of increasing complexity. Results are grouped as fluent (28 to 40), developing (20 to 27) or struggling (0 to 19) decoders.
tools.who: Year 1 teachers checking the effect of their phonics teaching, and anyone deciding which students need phonics intervention.
tools.access: Free with a teacher sign-in
tools.note: Designed for students who have had at least 18 months of systematic synthetic phonics teaching.

tools.name: Year 1 Number Check
tools.by: Australian Government, on the Mathematics Hub
tools.delivery: One-to-one interview, online or on paper
tools.time: Not stated. Choose the 20-item check or the shorter 12-item check.
tools.tells: Whether a student is developing the number and counting knowledge expected in Year 1, including numeral identification, number sequences, skip counting, subitising, counting, addition and subtraction.
tools.who: Year 1 teachers who want an early look at which students may need extra support in number.
tools.access: Free
tools.note: Aligned to the Australian Curriculum: Mathematics Version 9.

tools.name: CC2: Castles and Coltheart Test 2
tools.by: MOTIf, Macquarie University (Anne Castles and colleagues)
tools.years: Ages 6 to 11 and a half (Australian norms)
tools.time: Not stated. Up to 120 words, stopping after five errors in a row of each type.
tools.tells: Whether a reading difficulty lies in sounding out (nonwords such as gop), in recognising whole words (irregular words such as yacht), or in both. Scores are compared with more than 1000 Australian children.
tools.who: Intervention teachers, learning support staff and specialists working out why a student is struggling to read words.
tools.access: Free PDF to print (you give a few details). A paid digital version is also available.

tools.name: LeST: Letter Sound Test
tools.time: Not stated. 51 single letters and letter combinations.
tools.tells: Exactly which letters and letter combinations a student can sound out on their own, so you know which to teach next.
tools.who: Teachers and tutors planning phonics teaching or intervention for one student.
tools.access: Free PDF to print (you give a few details). A paid digital version is also available.

tools.name: DiRT: Diagnostic Reading Test for Nonwords
tools.tells: Which of more than 60 letter-sound rules a student can apply when reading made-up words. Where the CC2 shows whether nonword reading is a problem, the DiRT shows which rules are missing.
tools.who: Intervention staff who need a detailed map of the letter-sound rules to teach.
tools.access: Free PDF to print (you give a few details)

tools.name: LIDT: Letter Identification Test
tools.tells: Whether a student knows that upper and lower case forms, such as d and D, are the same letter.
tools.who: Teachers of beginning readers, and anyone checking the earliest building blocks for an older struggling reader.
tools.access: Free PDF to print (you give a few details)

tools.name: LetPos: Letter Position Test
tools.tells: Whether a student mixes up the order of letters inside words, such as reading slime as smile. It is particularly useful for screening for letter position dyslexia.
tools.who: Specialists and intervention teachers who see a student making anagram-style reading errors.
tools.access: Free PDF to print (you give a few details)

tools.name: TOC: Test of Orthographic Choice
tools.years: Compared with students in the same year level
tools.time: Not stated. 30 items and two practice items.
tools.tells: How well a student recognises correct spellings by sight. The student chooses the real word from a pair that sound the same, such as doar and door.
tools.who: Teachers and specialists who want to know whether a student is storing whole-word spellings.
tools.access: Free PDF to print (you give a few details)

tools.name: TERC: Test of Everyday Reading Comprehension
tools.by: MOTIf, Macquarie University (Genevieve McArthur and colleagues)
tools.time: Not stated. 10 items of increasing difficulty.
tools.tells: Whether a student's reading is good enough for everyday tasks, such as ordering from a canteen menu or following the instructions on a medicine bottle.
tools.who: Teachers and specialists working with older struggling readers, where functional reading matters.
tools.access: Free PDF to print (you give a few details). A paid digital version is also available.

tools.name: DiSTs: Diagnostic Spelling Test for Sounds
tools.tells: Whether a student can write the letter or letters for common English sounds when they hear each sound on its own.
tools.who: Teachers planning early spelling teaching, and intervention staff checking the basics.
tools.access: Free PDF to print (you give a few details). A paid digital version is also available.

tools.name: DiSTn: Diagnostic Spelling Test for Nonwords
tools.tells: Which of more than 40 sound-letter rules a student can apply when spelling made-up words.
tools.who: Anyone who needs to know exactly which spelling rules to teach a student or a group.
tools.access: Free PDF to print (you give a few details)

tools.name: DiSTi: Diagnostic Spelling Test for Irregular Words
tools.tells: How well a student has stored the spellings of whole words that cannot be worked out from sound-letter rules.
tools.who: Teachers and specialists comparing a student's irregular word spelling with others in the same year level.
tools.access: Free PDF to print (you give a few details). A paid digital version is also available.

tools.name: DiST-m: Diagnostic Spelling Test for Morphology
tools.years: From around Year 3 through secondary school
tools.tells: Which common suffixes and morphological spelling rules, such as past tense -ed, a student has learned. There are no published norms, but the error analysis shows what to teach.
tools.who: Teachers deciding which morphological spellings to focus on in class or in intervention.
tools.access: Free PDF to print (you give a few details)

tools.name: MAAST: Macquarie Advanced Adult Spelling Test
tools.tells: How well an adult spells difficult words that are commonly misspelled.
tools.who: Those working with adults, including in tertiary and adult education.
tools.access: Free PDF to print (you give a few details)

tools.name: RAT: Reading Anxiety Tests
tools.delivery: Questionnaire, completed by the student or a parent
tools.tells: Whether a child, adolescent or adult has raised levels of anxiety about reading. There are five versions, including parent-report forms.
tools.who: Wellbeing staff, psychologists and intervention teachers who suspect a struggling reader is also anxious about reading.
tools.access: Free PDFs to print. The parent report for children also has a digital version.

tools.name: NeST: negative evaluations about reading
tools.delivery: Questionnaire, with child, parent and teacher versions
tools.tells: Whether a primary student feels they have been judged negatively about their reading by peers, teachers or parents. There are no norms, but the answers give insight into how the student sees themselves.
tools.who: Teachers and wellbeing staff supporting a student whose confidence in reading is low.
tools.access: Free PDF to print (you give a few details)

tools.name: Australian norms for the TOWRE
tools.delivery: Used with the Test of Word Reading Efficiency
tools.tells: How an Australian primary student's score on the 1999 TOWRE compares with Australian children. Best used in the second half of the school year.
tools.who: Specialists who already own the original TOWRE, which is a paid test.
tools.access: Free PDF of the norms. The TOWRE itself is sold separately.
tools.note: The norms are for the original 1999 TOWRE, not TOWRE-2.

tools.name: BAPPA-F and BAPPA-R: plural processing in aphasia
tools.tells: How well a person with aphasia produces plurals, and whether word frequency or regularity affects it.
tools.who: Speech pathologists working with adults. These two are not school assessments, and are listed so the suite is complete.
tools.access: Free PDF to print (you give a few details)

tools.name: Acadience Reading K-6
tools.years: Foundation to Year 6 (American Kindergarten to Grade 6)
tools.delivery: Mostly one-to-one. Maze can be given to a whole class.
tools.time: A few minutes per student, with brief timed measures
tools.tells: Which students are at risk of reading difficulty and which skills to target, through measures of first sounds, letter naming, phoneme segmentation, nonsense word reading, oral reading fluency with retell, and Maze.
tools.who: Schools wanting benchmark screening three times a year, with progress monitoring forms for students receiving extra support.
tools.access: Free download from the Acadience Resource Hub. The online data system is paid.

tools.name: Acadience Math
tools.years: Foundation to Year 6 (American Kindergarten to Grade 6)
tools.delivery: Early numeracy measures are one-to-one. Computation and problem-solving measures can be given to a group.
tools.tells: Which students are on track in early numeracy, computation and problem solving, and whether intervention is making a difference.
tools.who: Schools that want maths screening to sit beside their reading screening, and maths intervention teams tracking progress.
tools.access: Free download from the Acadience Resource Hub. The online data system is paid.
tools.note: Aligned to American standards, so check the fit with your scope and sequence.

tools.name: The rest of the Acadience family
tools.years: Preschool to Year 12, depending on the measure
tools.delivery: Depends on the measure. Reading 7-8 and 9-12 are group-administered.
tools.tells: Beyond Reading K-6 and Math there is Reading Pre-K (PELI) for early childhood, Reading 7-8 and 9-12 for comprehension and fluency, RAN (rapid automatised naming) for Foundation and Year 1, Spelling for Foundation to Year 3, Reading Survey for testing out of year level, and Reading Diagnostic for a closer look at phonemic awareness, word reading, comprehension, fluency and oral language.
tools.who: Schools already using Acadience that want to extend it to younger or older students, or to look more closely at students flagged by screening.
tools.access: Materials are listed in the Resource Hub. Check each one, as some are sold through the Acadience store.

tools.name: CUBED-3
tools.by: Language Dynamics Group (Douglas Petersen and Trina Spencer)
tools.focus: Oral language, decoding and reading comprehension
tools.tells: How a student is going in both halves of reading. The Narrative Language Measures look at listening and reading comprehension through story retelling, and the decoding measures look at phonemic awareness, orthographic mapping and decoding.
tools.who: Schools that want a language measure alongside their decoding screener, which most free tools do not offer.
tools.access: Free paper and pencil version to download for personal use. The digital version is paid.

tools.name: PAST: Phonological Awareness Screening Test
tools.years: Foundation onwards, including older struggling readers
tools.tells: How far a student's phonological awareness has developed, from syllables through to manipulating individual phonemes, and how automatic it is.
tools.who: Teachers and intervention staff checking whether weak phonemic awareness sits behind a student's reading difficulty.
tools.access: Free download (four forms, with instructions)
